findings.title: Certificate expires in 9 days

findings.title: Deprecated protocol version negotiated (TLS 1.1)
findings.description: The session negotiated TLS 1.1, which RFC 8996 formally deprecates. It lacks AEAD cipher suites and modern signature algorithms, and is vulnerable to BEAST and Lucky13 when CBC suites are in use.

standards.requirement: TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 MUST NOT be used
Servers shall be configured to support TLS 1.2 and should support TLS 1.3
Deprecated TLS versions and weak ciphers must be disabled on government infrastructure

remediation.summary: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1; require TLS 1.2 as a minimum.
remediation.exchange: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1 via the SCHANNEL registry keys, then reboot.
remediation.risk_of_change: May break clients older than roughly 2015.

shap_contributions.human_readable: MTA relay: opportunistic TLS per RFC 7435

findings.title: Expired self-signed certificate presented
findings.description: The server presented a self-signed certificate whose validity period ended 47 days ago.
findings.severity_adjustment_reason: Downgraded from HIGH to INFO: port 25 is MTA-to-MTA relay, where TLS is opportunistic (RFC 7435) and the sender has no trust anchor for the receiver. Encrypting with an unvalidated certificate still beats cleartext.

standards.requirement: Opportunistic security: unauthenticated encryption is acceptable where authentication is impossible

remediation.summary: No action required for opportunistic relay, though a valid certificate would enable DANE or MTA-STS.

findings.title: STARTTLS capability stripped in transit
findings.description: The server's EHLO response advertised STARTTLS as '250-XXXXXXXA' — the capability keyword overwritten in place with a same-length placeholder. This is the signature of an on-path attacker removing the upgrade option. The client then proceeded in cleartext and authenticated.

standards.requirement: Mail submission and access MUST use TLS with certificate validation
A server MUST NOT advertise plaintext AUTH mechanisms before TLS

remediation.summary: Require TLS on submission; move users to implicit TLS on port 465; rotate every credential observed in this capture.
remediation.risk_of_change: Clients that cannot do TLS will stop working, which is the point.

findings.title: Account credentials transmitted in cleartext
findings.description: An AUTH LOGIN exchange completed before any TLS handshake. The username and password were recoverable by any observer on the path, including us.

standards.requirement: Mail submission and access MUST use TLS with certificate validation
A server MUST NOT advertise plaintext AUTH mechanisms before TLS

remediation.summary: Treat the exposed accounts as compromised and rotate immediately. Then enforce TLS before AUTH.

findings.severity_adjustment_reason: Raised from HIGH to CRITICAL: mail access port: a failed or skipped upgrade exposes credentials.

standards.requirement: Mail submission and access MUST use TLS with certificate validation
A server MUST NOT advertise plaintext AUTH mechanisms before TLS

remediation.summary: Set the client to require TLS, and refuse plaintext AUTH server-side.
